g0.rationale: Section 2.2 five-step test. Step 1: directions located (aggregated dm/retailer copy, packet confidence moderate). Step 2: three stated modes. (a) 'Als Haarmaske: auf das nasse Haar auftragen, 3 Minuten einwirken lassen und gruendlich ausspuelen' - stated contact time and rinse -> QUALIFIES. (b) 'Als Leave-in-Pflege ... nicht ausspuelen' -> fails, not rinsed. (c) 'Auch als Over-Night-Pflege verwendbar' -> fails, leave-on overnight, which is separately an excluded form on its own. Step 3: exactly one mode qualifies -> classify that mode, multi_use = true, uncovered modes named. Charter F1 names Balea Aqua Hyaluron 3 in 1 among the live multi-use boundary cases resolved as eligible mode-scoped.
evidenceSignals: multi_use: true
multi_use_covered_mode: post_shampoo_rinse_out_mask
multi_use_uncovered_modes: [leave_in, overnight_leave_on]
multi_use_directions_source: packet directions block, aggregated dm/retailer copy (confidence moderate - a documented sourcing gap on the directions leg)
Note: mode (c) is a form the charter excludes outright when it is a product's ONLY mode; here it is one uncovered mode among several, and section 2.2 covers only the qualifying mask mode
The 3-minute contact time is protocol metadata with zero classification credit

tailMarker.anomalyNote: Resolved, no anomaly (rank 9, and seven substantive entries precede it). Decisive consequence on the tail side: ISOAMYL LAURATE (10), BEHENTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE (11) and CETRIMONIUM CHLORIDE (12) all carry zero structural credit, so the formula's cationic breadth counts as one species, not three. The above-tail segment is humectant-dominated, which is what drives the profile.

conditioningLevel.evidenceScope: Above-tail segment (ranks 1-8) of the exact-market INCI; formula-only structural position.
conditioningLevel.rationale: Exactly one of the three structural signals is satisfied, which the section 9.1 threshold assigns to moderate. E2 ceiling: architecture, not delivered conditioning.
evidenceSignals: S1 not satisfied: DISTEAROYLETHYL HYDROXYETHYLMONIUM METHOSULFATE (4) is the only cationic species above the tail; BEHENTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE (11) and CETRIMONIUM CHLORIDE (12) are tail-side
S2 satisfied: CETEARYL ALCOHOL at rank 2, immediately after AQUA
S3 not satisfied: HELIANTHUS ANNUUS HYBRID OIL (8) is the only non-fatty-alcohol lipid above the tail; ISOAMYL LAURATE (10) is tail-side (and would be a light, weight-neutral ester in any case)
Not counted: no cationic polymer, no silicone, no protein anywhere in the formula
conditioningLevel.derivation: Section 9.1 S1/S2/S3 counting on the above-tail slice; 1 of 3 -> moderate.
thresholdReasoning: Why moderate, not high: high requires >= 2 signals; only S2 fires. The two additional cationics that would have satisfied S1 sit two and three ranks below the marker.
Why moderate, not low: low requires none of the three, and S2 is satisfied by CETEARYL ALCOHOL at rank 2. 'Exactly one satisfied signal' is explicitly moderate.

A fifteen-entry list with a nine-rank tail marker means the above-tail segment is eight entries - short but not minimal; five of those eight are humectant-class, which the structural signals do not index at all.
counterSignals: The formula is humectant-dominated above the tail, so field 1 (a cationic/lipid structural index) understates what this product is actually built around - that content is carried by fields 3 and 5 instead
CITRIC ACID (15) is tail-side pH context with no credit and is never a tail marker

weightPotential.rationale: The high anchor's required base fails on cationic breadth and the low anchor fails on its fatty-alcohol conjunct, leaving the residual. E2 ceiling.
evidenceSignals: High base leg 1 fails: one cationic species above the tail
High base leg 2 satisfied: CETEARYL ALCOHOL (2) in the top three
Both alternatives fail anyway: no R4b heavy lipid above the tail (sunflower hybrid oil at 8 is mid-band at most), and no silicone anywhere in the formula
Low anchor leg 1 satisfied: a single cationic species above the tail
Low anchor leg 2 FAILS: CETEARYL ALCOHOL (2) is a cetearyl-class fatty alcohol in the top three
Low anchor leg 3 satisfied: no R4b heavy lipid above the tail
weightPotential.derivation: Section 9.2: high fails on the base and on both alternatives; low fails on leg 2 -> moderate residual.
thresholdReasoning: Why moderate, not low: two of the three low-anchor conjuncts hold, but the anchor is a conjunction and cetearyl alcohol at rank 2 falsifies leg 2. This product is, on any intuitive reading, one of the lighter formulas in the set - and the anchor cannot say so, because a rank-2 cetearyl alcohol is near-universal in the category (lexicon family 2: presence carries no signal at all, only relative position and breadth do).
Why moderate, not high: the base fails and no alternative exists.
Conflict fallback not applicable (no formula-only high).
counterSignals: The product is directed for use as a leave-in and even overnight, which points at a light finish; that is a directions fact and G2 bars it from crossing into a comparison property, so it was recorded and not used
'Aqua Hyaluron' positioning is not weight evidence
ISOAMYL LAURATE would be a high-spreading light ester if it counted - it is tail-side and does not
limitations: The low anchor's fatty-alcohol conjunct is doing all the work here, and the lexicon's own note that a rank-2 cetearyl alcohol is category-universal suggests that conjunct will keep almost every mask out of 'low'. Worth calibration attention alongside the standard's open question 1.

careDirection.evidenceScope: Full ingredient list; comparative emphasis only, never a user-state assertion (G6).
careDirection.rationale: No protein-class species exists at any rank, so no R5 route is possible and the material direction is the coherent humectant/conditioning architecture the formula carries - D6's honest default, and here positively rather than residually supported. E2 ceiling; the wording is a humectant-forward comparative direction, never proven hydration.
evidenceSignals: Zero hydrolyzed proteins, peptides, keratin tokens, or cationised proteins at any rank

Coherent above-tail humectant/conditioning architecture: CETEARYL ALCOHOL (2), GLYCERIN (3), DISTEAROYLETHYL HYDROXYETHYLMONIUM METHOSULFATE (4), PANTHENOL (5), ALOE BARBADENSIS LEAF JUICE POWDER (6), SODIUM HYALURONATE (7), HELIANTHUS ANNUUS HYBRID OIL (8)
careDirection.derivation: Section 9.3: material-R5 test fails at its first condition (no qualifying species exists); balanced is gated on the same route; -> moisture.
thresholdReasoning: Why moisture, not protein: no protein-class species exists in the formula at all.

Why moisture, not balanced: balanced requires the material R5 route as a precondition. Note that this product would satisfy the balanced test's humectant branch easily - it fails only on the protein leg, which is the correct behaviour: balanced is never a 'neither' or 'strong-in-one-direction' bucket.
Confidence high: resolved tail marker, complete list, vacuous protein side, and D4 does not fire.
Section 9.3.1 is worth restating here: care_direction: moisture and primary_focus: moisture are different tests at different bars, and this is one of the rare products that clears both.
counterSignals: 'Aqua Hyaluron' naming aligns with the value, which is coincidence rather than evidence - claims are barred from care_direction
limitations: No claims summary; irrelevant for this field under section 11 step 4.

repairSupportLevel.evidenceScope: Full ingredient list; comparative route potential, never measured repair.

No R5 species at any rank
Explicit non-upgraders present: PANTHENOL (5), SODIUM HYALURONATE (7), CITRIC ACID (15)
repairSupportLevel.derivation: Section 9.4: high fails, medium fails -> low.
thresholdReasoning: Why low, not medium: no protein/peptide/keratin film route at any rank.
Why low, not high: no named bond chemistry.
This product makes no repair claim, so none of the three mask-delta inflation risks is even tempting here - it is the clean negative control for repair in the set.

primaryFocus.evidenceScope: Above-tail humectant cluster plus the section 9.5.2 hierarchy; humectant-forward comparative direction only.
primaryFocus.rationale: No richer special-purpose route wins, and the D5 cluster guard is met on all four criteria by a four-member above-tail cluster that is genuinely disjoint from the emollient base. E2 wording, binding: a humectant-forward comparative direction - never 'hydrates', never proven hydration, never a moisture-delivery claim.
evidenceSignals: Step 3 repair fails: no R5, no bond token
Step 3 curl_support fails: one cationic above the tail, no cationic polymer, no curl positioning
Step 3 color_care fails: no candidate, no positioning
Step 3 lightness fails: weight_potential is moderate, not low - so this product cannot take the lightness route despite its leave-in modes

Step 4 moisture, criterion 1 satisfied: GLYCERIN (3), PANTHENOL (5), ALOE BARBADENSIS LEAF JUICE POWDER (6), SODIUM HYALURONATE (7) - four distinct R9 humectants above the tail, three of them non-glycerin, against a bar of >= 3 with >= 2 non-glycerin

Criterion 2 satisfied: this is M5, not M1 - the only emollients above the tail are a rank-2 fatty alcohol and one sunflower oil, so there is no rich R1/R4 architecture for the moisture reading to be a disguised version of
Criterion 3 satisfied: no richer special-purpose route wins - repair, curl_support, color_care and lightness all failed
Criterion 4 satisfied: no hydrolyzed proteins exist to be miscounted
primaryFocus.derivation: Section 9.5.2 steps 1-4 in order; the D5 guard of section 9.5.3 applied in full. focus_care_verdict = moisture_supported: a coherent humectant cluster plus conditioning support meets the guard.
thresholdReasoning: Why moisture, not general: the guard is met on all four criteria with margin. Even discounting ALOE as a weak reconstituted-powder member (lexicon family 7 says count at most once, never as a strong member), the cluster is still three distinct members with two non-glycerin - exactly the bar - so the value survives the most conservative member accounting.
Why moisture, not smoothing: step 6 is below step 4, and its architecture conjunct fails anyway (no silicone, no substantive polymer, one lipid).
Why moisture, not shine: no optical-emphasis architecture and no gloss positioning.

Confidence high: section 9.5.3's confidence rule grants high for >= 3 distinct qualifying humectants above the tail with at least one within the first five ranks of the full list (GLYCERIN at 3 and PANTHENOL at 5 both qualify), a resolved tail marker, and no competing route. All three conditions hold.
claim_role = not_applicable: no claims summary. The 'Aqua Hyaluron' name would have corroborated but was not needed and cannot create a route.
counterSignals: Glycerin's rank carries no moisture signal on its own - it is a category base ingredient present regardless of positioning (lexicon family 7). The cluster clears without it
ALOE derived from juice powder is unquantifiable from the list and is counted once as a weak member
Hair-fibre hydration outcomes are weakly evidenced (lexicon W1); this is a comparative architecture direction, never an efficacy claim
limitations: The D5 guard's own open question (lexicon open item 3: whether the >= 3 cluster survives once glycols and aloe are discounted) is live here. It does survive on this product, which is a useful data point.
No claims summary was needed for any leg of this decision.
